rationale: Feedback-only product that narrows the active Candidate's exposure using source structure, without changing any map object. Comparing how the leader's and the peer's dependency vectors are computed shows why the N<=3 Thrifty equality exemption is sound in the owner-led case and why the recovery-led case is the one that can split: a peer recomputes with updateAttributes starting from the leader's transmitted deps vector and only increases components, and it skips the instance owner's row, so with a single fast-quorum peer the merged vector (componentwise maximum) equals that peer's vector whenever the leader is also the owner, and the leader installs that same merged vector on commit. When the leader is not the owner (recovery sub-case 5/6 restarts phase 1 for another replica's instance), the leader and the peer each skip the owner's row but add their own knowledge to their own rows, so the leader can contribute a component on the leader's row that the peer lacks while the peer contributes one on a different row: the merged vector is then strictly greater than both records and is held only by the leader after its fast commit.

feedback.answered: The exemption's reachable window is now located on sources. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given: it starts from the received deps vector, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and for every other row raises deps[q] to the highest conflicting instance known locally (S7-attributes). A pre-accepting peer therefore returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise; with one peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's merge equals that peer's vector, and the fast-commit branch installs the merged vector into the leader's own record (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). In that owner-led case the committed vector is held at the same vbal by both members of the fast quorum, so a recovery quorum (SlowQuorumSize = 2) must intersect one of them and sees the committed vector. The exemption is therefore not automatically unsafe. The case that can split is a phase 1 restarted for an instance whose owner is another replica (handlePrepareReply sub-case 5 or 6 calls startPhase1 with PreAccept.Replica = owner and LeaderId = recovering replica, S15-handlePrepareReply, S8-handlePropose-startPhase1). There the leader and the peer both skip the owner's row but raise their own rows from their own conflict tables, so the leader can contribute a component on its own row that the peer does not have while the peer contributes another: the merged vector is then strictly greater than either record and is held only by the committing leader, while the peer keeps its smaller vector at the same ballot (S9-handlePreAccept, S10-handlePreAcceptReply).
remaining: whether a recovery whose slow quorum contains the differing peer rather than the committed leader re-proposes the peer's smaller vector for the instance (the highest-vbal selection cannot separate them because both records carry the pre-accept ballot as vbal) (S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether the already-committed leader then refuses the later Commit and keeps the larger vector, freezing two committed vectors for one instance (handleCommit returns early for Status >= COMMITTED) (S13-handleCommit)
whether the two vectors order conflicting instances differently, since the difference is a dependency component on a row whose conflicting command may not yet be committed at the peer (S20-exec)

whether the recovery-led fast commit is reachable with a single peer reply inside the exempted configuration, that is whether an N=3 deployment with a non-owner recovery is a supported history (S24-runReplica-epaxos, S21-quorum-sizes)
feedback.rationale: This refines, rather than replaces, the earlier correction: the merged vector is what gets committed, and the question is whether any other replica holds it at the same vbal. The owner-led case is now explained (a single peer's vector dominates and is adopted by both), which is consistent with the source comment that equality need not be checked there. The recovery-led case remains open and is the discriminator a controlled schedule would settle; recording it here keeps the map stable and leaves the Candidate's proposition intact while making the next construction step concrete. Nothing in the requirement, the observed behaviors or the previously explained Candidate is weakened.

unknowns: whether the recovery-led (LeaderId != owner) variant of the exempted N=3 fast path is reachable with exactly one pre-accept reply, since that is the variant where the merged vector can be held only by the committing leader (S15-handlePrepareReply, S8-handlePropose-startPhase1, S10-handlePreAcceptReply)

whether a recovery that reaches only the differing peer re-proposes the peer's smaller vector and re-commits it, and whether the already-committed leader then refuses the later Commit because handleCommit returns early for Status >= COMMITTED (S15-handlePrepareReply, S13-handleCommit)

whether the differing dependency component changes the execution order of conflicting instances (it decides whether the instance waits for a command on that row), and therefore whether the split is state-visible rather than only record-visible (S20-exec)
